perspective:
I am Harold Padilla, a Latino man, a Project Manager; I know my own background and see myself as an empathetic, people-oriented person. I know Arthur Begum as a police officer and a friend/colleague whom I rely on for advice.

- I felt frustrated and anxious about my project’s progress. I believed my team was not performing well because they lacked motivation.
- I arranged and attended a coffee-shop meeting with Arthur. I told him my team seemed unmotivated and it was affecting progress, and that I was at my wit’s end.
- Arthur told me motivation can be tricky and asked if I had tried understanding what drives each team member individually. I admitted I had been focusing on project goals and deadlines, not personal motivations.
- Arthur advised one-on-one conversations and helping people feel valued and understood. I said I would try and felt more hopeful.
- Afterward, I felt hopeful and relieved and believed Arthur’s advice would help. I told my team we would have quick one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each of them and work better together.
- Team Member 1 said that could be helpful. Team Member 2 said they were open to it. I said I would schedule time with each of them and wanted us to make the project a success together.
- I then noticed the team still was not responding well. I felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future.
- I told Arthur I had tried his suggestions but the team still was not responding. Arthur said there might be deeper issues and asked if I had considered underlying problems. I had not.
- Arthur told me there could be personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that I might need to dig deeper. I said I would set up another round of meetings and thanked him.
- Feeling determined and focused, I believed there might be underlying team issues I had not addressed. I held one-on-one meetings and asked team members to share concerns or problems.
- Team Member 1 told me there was tension between a few people, affecting work; they did not specify who. I said I would look into resolving conflicts and asked if there was anything else.
- Team Member 2 told me they felt overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, making motivation hard. I said I understood, would see if tasks could be redistributed, and that their well-being was important.
- Feeling optimistic and empowered, I believed addressing individual concerns would improve performance. I told the team we would have regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive, open environment.
- Team Member 1 said that sounded great and would help. Team Member 2 agreed and said it was good that concerns were being addressed. I said I was glad and that their input and well-being are crucial to our success.
